key_insight: Sparse reward estimation can make private RLHF error depend on the number of relevant features s* rather than polynomially on the full model dimension d.
engineering_relevance: For high-dimensional reward models with sparse preference structure, this approach offers a potentially better privacy–utility trade-off than dense private estimation.
method: Model pairwise preferences using Bradley–Terry–Luce with an s*-sparse reward parameter.
Develop Sample-DP and randomized-response Label-DP estimators.
Prove squared parameter-error bounds of Õ(s*/n + s*²/(n²ε²)) for Sample-DP and Õ(s*/n + s*/(nε²)) for Label-DP.
evidence_signal: Experiments on sentiment generation and safety alignment benchmarks report better privacy–utility trade-offs than dense baselines; the abstract provides no numerical gains.
watch_item: Benefits rely on sparse reward structure, and Label-DP protects preference labels rather than entire training records.
paper_title: Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation with Preference Feedback
